usageNotes: Use this to retrieve pending (unapplied) configuration changes for an LXC container on a remote PVE cluster — changes that have been queued but not yet activated, typically requiring a container restart to take effect. The caller needs Resource.Audit privilege on the remote's guest resource. If the container's node is not specified, PDM resolves it automatically; supply the node parameter to skip that lookup or to disambiguate when the same VMID exists on multiple nodes.

examples.summary: Get pending config for LXC 201 on remote 'pve-hetzner', auto-resolved node

tips: A non-empty response means the container has staged config changes that differ from its running config — a restart is usually required to apply them.
If the container is actively running, pending changes will not be visible in the current/active config; always check this endpoint before and after making config edits.
Supplying the node query parameter avoids an extra cluster lookup and is slightly faster on large PVE clusters.
Returns null per spec when no pending changes exist — treat a null/empty response as 'no pending changes', not an error.
